title: R4: Bounded dispatch and affected verification
global_constraints: GC01: Script CEO owns dispatch, scheduling, gates, authoritative state, commits, and publication; no coordinating LLM is introduced.
GC02: The Codex path never executes OpenCode or silently changes runtime, model, reasoning effort, or role.
GC03: Every role receives explicit model and reasoning settings; operator, reviewer, and director have separate identities and permissions.
GC04: Plans, specs, prompts, ledger summaries, and implementation comments are English; product UI copy retains its established locale.
GC05: Codex workers inherit no brainstorming transcript; all required task context comes from versioned artifacts and explicit packages.
GC06: Operator-owned RED/GREEN and independent semantic review remain mandatory; mechanical green alone never approves a task or branch.
GC07: Raw evidence determines gates; RTK only changes the model-visible rendering and never the command exit code.
GC08: Unknown, malformed, stale, interrupted, or mismatched results never advance authoritative state.
GC09: Resume is confined to a recorded task family and role; unrelated tasks and closing use fresh contexts.
GC10: Parallel workers use distinct worktrees; shared plan writes, integration, and publication are serialized by scripts.
GC11: Existing user changes, unrelated branches, Codex sessions, credentials, and installed plugin caches are preserved.
GC12: Jev remains optional advisory inference; it cannot dispatch, select a tier, approve, route, or write the authoritative ledger.
GC13: Each new run confirms local-only or push-and-PR publication and concurrency at launch; resume retains those choices and no automatic merge is allowed.
GC14: Compatibility is claimed only for runtime/platform/toolchain combinations backed by the acceptance matrix.

tasks.title: Centralize correction routing and enforce dispatch budgets
tasks.summary: Remove unnecessary director hops while preserving independent semantic review and bounded recovery.
acceptance: Refresh the per-site dispatch inventory and assign each semantic invocation one owner. Flutter gate delegates review to the shared owner.

Route SEND_BACK directly to the coder when structured scope is in_scope and paths/contracts fit the approved task plus valid scope grants. Structural/uncertain/viability findings require director; malformed metadata blocks.

Default coder cycle allowances are [5,3,3], at most three cycles and eleven coder invocations. After each exhausted cycle return to director; pause after the third assessment or earlier unresolved ruling. Configure before run and persist counts across crashes, scope changes and corrective child tasks.
Gate infrastructure failure leaves a pending gate/review, not a new coding request. Classify transport attempts separately; never double-charge resumed/reconciled invocation identities.
Keep updated independent re-review candidate-bound. Scope changes use R3 canonical transactions. Reviewer cannot approve its own fixes.
Fixtures cover normal two-invocation path, in-scope fix without director, structural escalation, missing session, budget exhaustion, crash replay and duplicate Flutter review prevention.

Count external coder invocations, not internal RED/GREEN turns. Separate confirmed pre-start transport retries and infrastructure failures from coding failures; ambiguous post-start invocations are reconciled, never silently erased from the budget.

tasks.title: Build evidence-bound affected-test selection
tasks.summary: Compute tests from actual changes and dependency impact with conservative fallback.
acceptance: Inputs include actual base/head diff including deleted/renamed files, task scope, test paths, dependency reverse edges and toolchain rules. Output contains commands/tests/reasons/gaps, tree/config/environment hashes and policy version.
Include affected consumers, contracts and integration checks. A changed production path with no match is an explicit gap requiring broader tests.

Missing/stale graph, unknown language, dependency/build/test configuration, shared infrastructure or generated contract changes expand to full suite. Do not infer completeness from file-name proximity.
Provide initial Python unittest and Flutter/Dart rules with demonstrable mappings; unsupported Node/Rust/Go configurations retain full-suite descriptors until adapter evidence exists.
Use deterministic traversal and stable output; reject unsafe argv/path selectors and malformed graphs. Cover cycles, renames, deleted tests, transitive imports and shared-code changes.

Build a fresh Graphify 0.9.50 raw AST graph from an isolated baseline/candidate snapshot with `--no-cluster`; use only validated AST-origin imports/imports_from, validate source inventory and Dart/package/ Python module resolution, and fail closed to complete suites for missing/untrusted evidence. The old Graphify knowledge/context stage remains excluded.

tasks.title: Record baseline failures and explicit closing waivers
tasks.summary: Distinguish inherited failures from new regressions without silently relaxing completion.
acceptance: Capture suite/test identities, raw failures, baseline source/environment/command hashes before changed-code verification. Do not classify an unexplained failure as baseline merely because it is familiar.
Allow demonstrably unaffected work to continue; new regressions and ambiguous failures block affected work. Do not automatically add unrelated repairs to scope.

At closing rerun the required suites and compare evidence. Remaining proven baseline failures require an explicit user waiver bound to failure identities and final candidate; stale or broadened waivers are rejected.
Report completed-with-waived-baseline distinctly from green completion, preserving raw failing results. Never let a worker issue its own waiver or waive new regressions.
Cover renamed tests, changed error signatures, environment drift, new failures, unaffected task continuation and candidate-bound waiver expiry.

consumes: R3 evidence/candidate identity and script-owned state; recorded user waiver

tasks.title: Apply impact gates at task, integration and closing boundaries
tasks.summary: Wire selective verification without weakening final full-suite requirements.
acceptance: Task gate uses verified impact manifest, not coder-provided arbitrary test lists; static analysis and formatting retain required scope.
Recompute impact on each merged candidate; do not reuse isolated worktree success for a changed merged tree.
Closing requires every configured suite for every affected toolchain. Cache reuse needs identical tree/environment/commands/config; otherwise rerun.

Final new regressions block completion/publication and reopen work. Proven pre-existing failures require a valid candidate-bound user waiver; preserve a non-green, explicitly waived completion status. Unknown impact broadens test selection.
Update operator guidance to focused iteration and script-owned verification, explicitly overriding upstream pre-commit full-suite language only under this verified policy.
Fixtures simulate cross-task regression, stale evidence, configuration changes, no test matches, mixed toolchains and final failure.

Task/integration gates execute only validated manifest test argv for the exact candidate; baseline/closing execute full suites. Graphify or candidate drift rejects selective PASS, while analysis/format scope and the user checkout graphify-out remain untouched.

tasks.title: Add dispatch-cost audits, documentation and acceptance
tasks.summary: Strengthen skill-scripter and quantify execution cost without claiming savings from call counts alone.
acceptance: Skill-scripter requires every call site's role, trigger, frequency, budget, termination entry and keep/remove/merge decision, including dynamic calls and worker delegation.
Metrics separate semantic invocations, backend model turns, transport retries, Jev calls, input/output/cached tokens when available, latency and escaped-defect observations; unknown usage stays null.
Audit rejects newly introduced mechanical model routing and unbounded call loops; semantic calls carry a justification.
Record supersession of historical unbounded retry and ADR-0012 per-merge testing policy without erasing history.
Acceptance covers both backend fixtures, regression/quality gates and full final suites. Report measured results; do not assume fewer invocations proves savings.
